Standard naxps

Source: R/standard.R
naxp_standard.Rd

naxp_standard() gives one of the standard naxps built into every naxp library, and naxp_standards() lists them all.

Usage

naxp_standard(id, variant = "default")

naxp_standards()

Arguments

id

A single string: the standard's id, such as "uk-postcode".

variant

A single string: the variant's id. "default" or "" gives the default.

Value

  • naxp_standard(): a naxp.

  • naxp_standards(): a data frame with one row per variant, each standard's default first, and character columns id, name (for display), variant, pattern and notes (what the variant accepts and prints, in Markdown).

Details

The standard naxps are for widely used code systems such as postcodes. Each has an id, such as "uk-postcode", and one or more variants, one of which is "default". The id and the variant are matched without regard to ASCII case. Once published, a standard naxp never changes, so values encoded with it keep their meaning.

The standard naxps are described at https://naxp.org/standard/.

Examples

uk_postcode <- naxp_standard("uk-postcode")
naxp_encode(c("EC4M 7AA", "EC4M7AA", "B1 1AA"), uk_postcode)
#> <naxp_encoded[3]> \A\A?\9\X? \s!! \9\A\A | GIR \s!! 0AA
#> [1] EC4M 7AA EC4M 7AA B1 1AA  

naxp_standard("nl-postcode", "no-separator")
#> <naxp> \9\9\9\9 \s!? \A\A
#> Maximum encoded value: 6760000

naxp_standards()[, c("id", "variant")]
#>                   id           variant
#> 1        uk-postcode           default
#> 2        uk-postcode  padding-tolerant
#> 3        uk-postcode padding-canonical
#> 4            eircode           default
#> 5            eircode      no-separator
#> 6        nl-postcode           default
#> 7        nl-postcode      no-separator
#> 8        nl-postcode   hyphen-tolerant
#> 9  flight-designator           default
#> 10 flight-designator            strict
